intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including howler monkeys and toucans.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of hanging bridges and trails. Walk at canopy level to observe exotic birds, howler monkeys, and tropical flora up close. The iconic cone of Arenal Volcano provides a dramatic backdrop throughout the hike.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The park also features stunning Pacific beaches where you can relax after the wildlife walk.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on a guided day trek through Corcovado National Park. Encounter tapirs, peccaries, giant anteaters, and all four of Costa Rica's monkey species in their pristine natural habitat. This remote and raw experience is the pinnacle of eco-adventure in Central America.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport's affordable food court (sodas or fast food options, ~$8-12 USD) before or after baggage claim if hungry upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared shuttle in advance (~$15-25 USD) rather than a private taxi to save money. Have your hotel address printed or saved offline. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs, but use ATMs in town for better rates. February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect warm, sunny weather.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a free orientation walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the shoreline, watch for shorebirds and pelicans, and get your bearings. Collect a local map from the hotel reception.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local town or village on foot or by local bus (~$1 USD). Browse the central market or farmers' market for fresh tropical fruits (papaya, mango, pineapple — ~$2-4 USD). Pop into a local 'soda' (small traditional Costa Rican diner) to sample the culture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll on the beach. Watch for nesting sea turtles if the season aligns. Enjoy the resort's common outdoor areas. Head to a nearby budget-friendly soda or beachside shack for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Casado breakfast at the hotel or a nearby soda — gallo pinto (rice and beans), eggs, and fresh juice (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from the market plus a light snack from a local vendor (~$3-5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local soda — try arroz con pollo or casado with fish (~$6-9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery and orientation day. Keep it relaxed. Ask hotel staff for trusted local recommendations for budget dining and upcoming eco-tours. Confirm zip-lining and wildlife tour bookings for later in the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along a nearby nature trail or beach. Look for howler monkeys, iguanas, coatis, and tropical birds. Bring binoculars if available. Many coastal areas in Costa Rica have free or low-cost public access trails. Depart by 6:00 AM for best wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife reserve (entry fees typically $5-18 USD for foreigners). Explore marked trails independently to save on guide fees. Look for sloths, toucans, and poison dart frogs in the canopy and undergrowth.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Rinse off and relax. Take an evening walk along the beach and stargaze — Costa Rica's coastal skies are spectacular in dry season.

meals.breakfast: Pack a self-prepared breakfast from market fruit and granola bars (~$2-3 USD) to eat on the trail
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from a local soda the night before — rice, beans, and plantains (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using resort kitchen facilities if available, or dine at a local soda (~$6-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing and closed-toe shoes for wildlife walks. Apply sunscreen and insect repellent (DEET-based for jungle areas). Carry 2 liters of water per person. Early mornings (5:30-8:00 AM) are the best time for wildlife activity.

day_by_day.morning: ZIP-LINING DAY! Book a budget zip-line tour through a local operator (compare prices — expect $40-70 USD for a multi-line course). Many operators offer free hotel pickup. Depart early to beat the heat. Zip-lining through Costa Rica's rainforest canopy is a bucket-list experience with incredible views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby hanging bridges walk or canopy walkway if included in the tour package or offered as an add-on (~$15-25 USD). Walk among the treetops and spot birds, monkeys, and sloths at eye level.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort tired but exhilarated. Treat yourself to a local Imperial beer (~$2 USD) or fresh coconut water from a roadside vendor. Share photos and stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Hearty gallo pinto with eggs and coffee at a nearby soda before departure (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Many zip-line tours include lunch — if not, grab a casado at a local soda near the tour site (~$6-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebrate the adventure day at a slightly nicer budget restaurant — try fresh grilled fish or shrimp (~$10-14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-line tours at least 1-2 days in advance. Compare prices between operators and look for combo deals. Weight and health restrictions may apply. Secure all loose items (glasses, hats, phones) before each line. Many operators provide GoPro footage for an additional fee (~$15-20 USD) — worth considering for memories.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or tide pool exploration along the coast near the resort. Many beaches in Costa Rica have free access to vibrant marine life. Rent snorkel gear from a local shop (~$8-12 USD for the day) or join a budget group snorkel tour (~$25-40 USD including equipment).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or frog sanctuary (~$10-15 USD entry). These small eco-attractions are common near beach towns and offer close-up encounters with poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, and other exotic species. Very educational and photogenic.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset kayaking along the coast or in a nearby estuary (~$15-25 USD for 2-hour rental). Paddle through mangroves and watch for crocodiles, herons, and roosting birds at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit smoothie and toast at a beachside café (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Ceviche and patacones (fried plantains) from a beachside vendor or local soda (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Fish tacos or a seafood platter at a casual beachfront restaurant (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Check local tide charts for the best snorkeling conditions — low tide reveals more tide pools. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only when snorkeling to protect Costa Rica's marine ecosystems. The butterfly garden is great for photography — bring your camera or phone in a waterproof case.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby waterfall. Many Costa Rican regions have stunning accessible waterfalls with modest entry fees ($3-10 USD). Hike through the jungle trail to reach the falls (1-3 hours round trip depending on location). Swim in the natural pool at the base — a refreshing and magical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the waterfall area or return via a different scenic trail. Look for wildlife along the path — toucans, monkeys, and leaf-cutter ants are commonly spotted. Take your time and enjoy the lush environment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Visit a local pulpería (corner store) to stock up on snacks, water, and budget supplies. Spend the evening relaxing on the beach or socializing with other travelers at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Pack a self-prepared breakfast — peanut butter sandwiches and bananas from the market (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the waterfall — packed rice, beans, and fruit (~$3-5 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget casado dinner at a local soda near the resort (~$6-9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes or sandals with grip for waterfall hikes — rocks can be slippery. Pack a dry bag for electronics. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. Some waterfalls require a short 4x4 road — check with the hotel about transportation options (shared taxi ~$10-15 USD round trip).

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend the morning at the beach. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) if available at the resort or a nearby rental shop (~$10-15 USD per hour). Great core workout with stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town more thoroughly. Visit a local artisan market or craft fair to browse handmade jewelry, wood carvings, and souvenirs. Bargain respectfully — prices are often negotiable. Budget $10-20 USD for small gifts and keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local cultural event if available (check community boards or ask hotel staff). Alternatively, join other travelers for a bonfire on the beach. Try a local bar for a happy hour Imperial or guaro sour (~$2-4 USD per drink).

meals.breakfast: Full gallo pinto breakfast with fresh juice at the hotel or nearby soda (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Chifrijo (rice, beans, chicharrones, pico de gallo) at a local bar or soda (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner using groceries from the local supermarket — pasta, vegetables, and local cheese (~$5-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to do laundry at a local laundromat (~$5-8 USD wash and fold) and reorganize your pack. Review your remaining budget and adjust plans if needed. Check in with family or friends back home using resort WiFi.

day_by_day.morning: Wildlife-focused boat tour through a nearby river, estuary, or mangrove system (~$25-45 USD for a shared group tour). These tours are outstanding for spotting American crocodiles, caimans, monkeys, sloths, and over 100 species of birds. Depart early for best wildlife activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture project (~$10-20 USD for a guided tour). Learn about sustainable agriculture in Costa Rica, sample fresh produce, and understand the country's commitment to eco-conscious living. Many farms offer chocolate or coffee tastings included in the tour.
day_by_day.evening: Night wildlife walk with a local guide (~$20-35 USD). Costa Rica's nocturnal wildlife is extraordinary — spot red-eyed tree frogs, Jesus lizards, tarantulas, and kinkajous. A headlamp and good walking shoes are essential.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at a soda before the boat tour — eggs, gallo pinto, and coffee (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Farm-fresh lunch at the organic farm if included, or a light soda meal (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Warm soup (sopa negra or black bean soup) and bread at a local restaurant — perfect after an evening walk (~$5-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the night wildlife walk through the hotel or a reputable local guide — do not wander jungle paths alone at night. Wear long sleeves and pants for the night walk to protect against insects. The boat tour is one of the best value wildlife experiences in Costa Rica — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Second zip-lining or canopy experience at a different operator if budget allows, OR try a thrilling white-water rafting excursion on a nearby river (~$45-75 USD for a half-day shared group tour on Class II-IV rapids). Costa Rica is world-renowned for its rafting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning adventure, visit a nearby hot spring if geologically accessible in your region (~$10-30 USD entry for budget springs). Soak tired muscles in natural thermal waters surrounded by jungle — a perfect recovery activity.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort. Write in a travel journal, review photos, and plan the final days of the trip. Watch the sunset from the beach with a cold drink.

meals.breakfast: Energy-packed breakfast before the adventure — eggs, toast, banana, and coffee (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Post-adventure lunch at a local soda — hearty casado with chicken or fish (~$6-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a casual budget restaurant for a change of pace (~$7-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: If choosing rafting, confirm the difficulty level matches your experience and comfort. All reputable operators provide safety gear and briefings. The hot springs recommendation depends on your specific location in Costa Rica — ask hotel staff for the nearest affordable option. Arenal region has the most famous hot springs if a day trip is feasible.

day_by_day.morning: Horseback riding through jungle trails or along the beach (~$30-50 USD for a 2-hour guided ride). This is a classic Costa Rican eco-adventure experience that covers terrain not accessible on foot. Look for wildlife from horseback — a unique perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local sea turtle conservation project or wildlife rescue center (~$10-20 USD donation/entry). Learn about Costa Rica's incredible conservation efforts. If timing aligns, volunteer for a morning or afternoon shift at a rescue center (often free in exchange for help).
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire and stargazing. Collect driftwood responsibly or join a group bonfire organized by the resort or fellow travelers. February's dry season skies offer exceptional stargazing conditions.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit plate at a beachside café (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Wrap or sandwich from a local bakery or café (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: BBQ on the beach — buy fresh fish or chicken from the market and grill at the resort if facilities allow (~$6-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Choose a reputable horseback riding operator that visibly cares for their horses (well-fed, appropriate saddles, not overworked). Wildlife rescue centers do important work — your entry fee directly supports animal rehabilitation. Bring a red-light headlamp for stargazing to preserve your night vision.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to a nearby national park or protected reserve not yet visited (e.g., Manuel Antonio, Corcovado, Tortuguero, or Monteverde depending on your base location). Depart by 6:00 AM via public bus or shared shuttle (~$5-20 USD). These parks are among the most biodiverse places on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Hire a certified local guide at the park entrance (~$20-30 USD for a half-day) for a dramatically improved wildlife-spotting experience — guides find animals that independent travelers consistently miss. Worth every colón.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and begin mentally preparing for the end of the trip. Share recommendations with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast to eat on the bus — granola bars, fruit, and a thermos of coffee (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Soda near the park entrance — casado or rice and beans (~$6-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — try a whole grilled snapper or lobster if budget allows (~$12-18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: National park entry fees for foreigners: $18-25 USD typically. Some parks (like Corcovado) require advance reservations — book online before the trip. Bring ALL essentials: water (3L), sunscreen, insect repellent, rain jacket, snacks, and a fully charged phone. This is likely your most memorable wildlife day.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or meditation on the beach (many resorts and local instructors offer free or donation-based sessions ~$5-10 USD). A peaceful and grounding way to begin your penultimate full day. Alternatively, take one final early-morning wildlife walk along a favorite trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and gift buying in the local town. Budget $15-30 USD for gifts: look for handmade crafts, locally produced coffee, dark chocolate bars, hot sauce, and small carved animals. Support local artisans rather than large souvenir chains.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with any travel friends made during the trip. Choose a restaurant with live music or a cultural performance if available. Reflect on the incredible 13-day journey through one of the world's most biodiverse countries.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional Costa Rican breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Ceviche and patacones at a beachside vendor — a final taste of coastal Costa Rica (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Group farewell dinner at a local restaurant — split a large seafood platter or try traditional olla de carne stew (~$10-15 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the day to settle any outstanding bills with the hotel, confirm your departure transportation for tomorrow, and pack your bags. Vacuum-seal dirty laundry to save space. Keep souvenirs in carry-on if fragile. Costa Rican coffee makes the best gift — buy at a local shop for better prices than the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Wake up for one last sunrise on the beach — a moment to treasure. Take a slow, mindful walk along the shoreline, collect a few shells as free souvenirs, and say goodbye to the Pacific (or Caribbean). Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort by the required time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, use remaining hours to visit any missed local spots, enjoy a final coffee at a beachside café, or simply relax. Arrange shared shuttle or public bus to Juan Santamaría International Airport (~$15-25 USD shared shuttle). Arrive at the airport 2-3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of zip-lining through rainforest canopies, wildlife encounters, pristine beaches, and the warmth of Pura Vida culture. Browse duty-free for any last-minute coffee or chocolate purchases at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at a local soda or the resort — savor every bite (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or a final soda meal near the resort before departure (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport food or on the plane — save remaining colones for airport snacks or exchange back to USD

day_by_day.notes: Exchange remaining Costa Rican colones back to USD at the airport (rates are acceptable for small amounts). Keep all receipts for any VAT refund claims if applicable. The departure tax is typically included in modern airline tickets — confirm with your airline. Leave a review for your favorite local guides, sodas, and tour operators to support the local economy. ¡Pura Vida!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on United flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked private shuttle or official taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind, and get oriented with the resort amenities. Light welcome drink at the resort bar if still open.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at the resort bar or a quick bite from a 24-hour soda (local diner) near the resort if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely light. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings, exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones, and get a good night's rest. Download offline maps of Costa Rica for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Spend the morning getting acquainted with the Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront surroundings. Take a relaxed stroll along the beach, dip in the ocean, and acclimate to the tropical climate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest coastal town for a self-guided exploration. Browse local artisan markets, pick up souvenirs, and get a feel for Costa Rican 'Pura Vida' culture. Stop by a local grocery or mini-super to stock up on snacks and water for the coming days.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail on the resort's beachfront terrace. Head to a nearby mid-range seafood restaurant for a traditional Costa Rican dinner featuring fresh catch of the day, rice, and beans.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – enjoy gallo pinto (rice and beans), tropical fruits, eggs, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Casual beachside soda – try a casado (rice, beans, salad, protein) for around $8–$12
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant near the resort – grilled mahi-mahi or red snapper with patacones (fried plantains), $15–$25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Use this day purely for recovery and orientation. Confirm shuttle or transport bookings for the Tortuguero trip on Day 3. Apply sunscreen generously and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private shuttle or organized tour transfer toward the Caribbean coast. Board a motorized canal boat at the Tortuguero embarkation point (La Pavona or Caño Blanco). Begin the **Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari** – glide through jungle canals spotting caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, sloths, and an abundance of tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat safari through the deeper canal networks of Tortuguero. After the safari, explore Tortuguero village on foot – a charming car-free town accessible only by boat or plane. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Visitor Center to learn about the park's famous green sea turtle nesting programs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Tortuguero village at a local restaurant. Take an optional guided night walk along the beach (February is early nesting season – check with local guides for turtle activity). Return to your overnight lodge in Tortuguero.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure or packed breakfast from resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local soda in Tortuguero village – rice, beans, fresh fish, $8–$12
meals.dinner: Budda Café or La Casona restaurant in Tortuguero village – Caribbean-style rice and beans with coconut milk, $12–$20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero requires an overnight stay due to distance. Book a mid-range jungle lodge such as Manatus Hotel or Tortuga Lodge in advance. Pack insect repellent, rain jacket, and waterproof bag for the boat safari. No roads access Tortuguero – all transport is by boat or small aircraft.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise kayak or canoe paddle through the quieter secondary canals of Tortuguero – the best time to spot wildlife before the heat of the day. Look for poison dart frogs, Jesus Christ lizards, and rare bird species like the great green macaw.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the return boat and shuttle back toward the base area. Travel northwest toward the **Arenal Volcano** region (approximately 3–4 hours). Check in to a mid-range lodge near La Fortuna, the gateway town to Arenal.
day_by_day.evening: Reward tired muscles with a soak at one of La Fortuna's famous natural hot springs (Baldi Hot Springs or Tabacón are popular mid-range options). Enjoy the volcanic thermal waters under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Tortuguero lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside soda during the transfer
meals.dinner: La Fortuna town center restaurant – try Restaurante Nene's or Don Rufino for traditional Costa Rican cuisine, $15–$25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Travel day between Tortuguero and Arenal. Confirm hot springs entry in advance (Baldi is ~$30–$40/person, Tabacón ~$60–$80 but worth budgeting for). Arenal Volcano views are best in the early morning before clouds roll in.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the **Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike** – trek through the lush primary and secondary rainforest on a network of hanging suspension bridges offering panoramic views of the volcano and forest canopy. Spot toucans, howler monkeys, and morpho butterflies. The hike covers approximately 3km with 16 bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off with a swim at La Fortuna Waterfall – a stunning 70-meter cascade accessible via a short steep trail (entrance ~$18). The turquoise pool at the base is perfect for a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna town for dinner and evening exploration. Browse the lively main street with its cafés, souvenir shops, and street food vendors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or lodge breakfast – gallo pinto, eggs, fresh tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near the hanging bridges or at the waterfall area – pick up supplies from a local market
meals.dinner: Kappa Restaurant or Restaurante Gecko in La Fortuna – wood-fired pizza or Costa Rican fusion, $12–$22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Start the hanging bridges hike early (7–8am) for best wildlife activity and cooler temperatures. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes and bring plenty of water. The waterfall trail has 500+ steps – take it at your own pace. Book hanging bridges tickets in advance (~$30/person for self-guided).

day_by_day.morning: Optional early morning guided birdwatching tour around Lake Arenal or the Arenal Observatory Lodge trails. The area is renowned for over 850 bird species. Alternatively, enjoy a peaceful morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal with views of the volcano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Arenal Eco Zoo or Arenal Natura ecological park to see reptiles, frogs, butterflies, and other wildlife up close in a controlled educational environment – great for wildlife enthusiasts. Spend the late afternoon relaxing at the lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hot springs for a final evening soak (try Eco Termales for a more intimate, less crowded experience, ~$40/person). Enjoy a farewell dinner in La Fortuna before preparing for travel to Monteverde.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast or local bakery – try Rainforest Bakery in La Fortuna for fresh pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Soda La Parada in La Fortuna – hearty casado lunch, $8–$12
meals.dinner: El Novillo Steakhouse in La Fortuna – local beef tenderloin with chimichurri, $18–$28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pack and prepare bags tonight for the morning move to Monteverde. The jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal to Monteverde is the most scenic and recommended route (~$25–$35/person, 3 hours total) – book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal to Monteverde – a scenic and memorable journey combining 4WD jeep, motorboat crossing, and another jeep up into the cloud forest mountains. Arrive in Santa Elena / Monteverde by midday. Check in to a cozy mid-range cloud forest lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Santa Elena town center on foot. Visit the Bat Jungle (educational exhibit about Costa Rica's 109 bat species), browse local coffee and chocolate shops, and sample artisan products. Stop by a local chocolate tour at Café Monteverde or Choco-Arte for a hands-on tasting experience (~$15).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a night tour of the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve or Santa Elena Reserve – the cloud forest transforms after dark with tree frogs, insects, and nocturnal mammals emerging. A certified naturalist guide makes the experience extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at La Fortuna lodge before the jeep-boat-jeep departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Santa Elena town upon arrival – Taco Taco or Orchid Coffee Shop, $8–$14
meals.dinner: Sofía Restaurant in Monteverde – contemporary Costa Rican 'Nuevo Latino' cuisine in a beautiful setting, $18–$28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Monteverde roads are unpaved and bumpy – the jeep-boat-jeep route via Lake Arenal is far more comfortable than the direct road. Bring a light fleece or jacket as Monteverde is significantly cooler than the coast (15–20°C). Night tours should be booked in advance (~$25–$35/person).

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of Monteverde: the **Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour** – soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. Experience multiple platforms, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views above the forest canopy shrouded in mist. The full circuit typically lasts 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline of zip-lining, visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a self-guided or guided afternoon hike through primary cloud forest. Walk the famous 'Continental Divide' trail and look for the elusive resplendent quetzal – February is an excellent month for quetzal sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a well-earned dinner in Santa Elena. Optionally, visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden at dusk or catch a local cultural performance at the town center.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – fuel up well before zip-lining
meals.lunch: Picnic or light snack near the reserve, or quick bite at the reserve's café
meals.dinner: Tree House Restaurant & Bar in Santa Elena – casual atmosphere, burgers, pasta, and local dishes, $12–$20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line tour for the early morning slot (8am) to catch the cloud forest in its most atmospheric misty state. Weight and age restrictions apply for zip-lining – confirm with the operator. Cloud Forest Reserve entrance is ~$25/person. Quetzal sightings are most likely between 6–9am along the Chomogo trail.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve – a community-managed reserve that is often less crowded than the main Monteverde reserve but equally spectacular. Hike the Sky Walk trails among epiphytes, orchids, and bromeliads. Look for three-wattled bellbirds, golden-browed chlorophonia, and other endemic cloud forest species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by private shuttle or public bus from Monteverde south toward **Manuel Antonio** on the Pacific coast (approximately 4–5 hours). The journey passes through the Central Valley and descends to the warm Pacific lowlands. Check in to a mid-range hotel in Manuel Antonio / Quepos area.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up and enjoy your first Pacific sunset of the trip from a beachside restaurant or bar in Manuel Antonio. The transition from cool cloud forest to warm tropical beach is one of Costa Rica's greatest contrasts.

meals.breakfast: Final cloud forest breakfast at the Monteverde lodge
meals.lunch: Roadside soda stop during the transfer – typical casado, $8–$10
meals.dinner: El Avión Restaurant in Manuel Antonio – dinner inside a converted 1954 Fairchild C-123 cargo plane with Pacific ocean views, $20–$35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Monteverde to Manuel Antonio shuttle in advance with Interbus or Grayline (~$45–$55/person). El Avión is a Manuel Antonio institution – reservations recommended. Enjoy the dramatic climate change between Monteverde and Manuel Antonio.

day_by_day.morning: Enter **Manuel Antonio National Park** for the **Guided Wildlife Tour** with a certified naturalist guide. Explore one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse parks, home to all four monkey species (squirrel, howler, white-faced capuchin, spider), two-toed and three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare titi monkey. Morning entry (6–8am) offers the best wildlife activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided wildlife tour, stay in the park to enjoy Manuel Antonio's pristine white-sand beaches. Playa Manuel Antonio and Playa Espadilla Sur are stunning – swim, snorkel, or simply relax under the shade of a palm tree. Keep an eye out for wildlife wandering onto the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Quepos town for a lively evening. Quepos has an excellent selection of restaurants, bars, and a vibrant local atmosphere. Explore the marina area and enjoy a sunset cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before park entry – hotel or a quick café near the park entrance
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the park's concession area or pack your own (no single-use plastics in the park)
meals.dinner: Gabriella's Restaurant in Quepos marina – fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and tropical cocktails, $15–$25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap – book entry tickets online in advance at sinac.go.cr. Park is closed on Mondays. Guided tours cost ~$50–$70/person but dramatically increase wildlife spotting success. Bring a dry bag for beach time and keep all food secured from monkeys.

day_by_day.morning: Optional sunrise kayak sea tour around the Manuel Antonio coastline and offshore islands – spot dolphins, sea turtles, and seabirds from the water. Alternatively, take a morning snorkeling trip to the coral reefs around Biesanz Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by shuttle from Manuel Antonio/Quepos south toward the **Osa Peninsula** and **Corcovado National Park** region (approximately 3–4 hours to Puerto Jiménez or Drake Bay). This is one of Costa Rica's most remote and wild destinations. Check in to an eco-lodge in the Osa Peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the remote jungle atmosphere of the Osa Peninsula. Enjoy dinner at the eco-lodge, which often uses locally sourced ingredients. Listen to the sounds of the rainforest at night – howler monkeys, tree frogs, and insects create an extraordinary natural symphony.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Manuel Antonio before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch during transfer or stop in Palmar Norte
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge dinner at your Osa Peninsula accommodation – typically included or semi-included at jungle lodges, $15–$25 if à la carte

day_by_day.notes: The Osa Peninsula is remote and requires advance planning. Mid-range eco-lodge options include Iguana Lodge, Bosque del Cabo, or Osa Preciosa. Roads to Puerto Jiménez are paved; Drake Bay access may require a boat transfer. Confirm all logistics with your lodge. Stock up on cash in Quepos as ATMs are scarce on the Osa.

day_by_day.morning: The grand finale of the wildlife experiences: the **Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition** – venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests with a certified guide. Trek through primary old-growth rainforest to spot tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, harpy eagles, and all four monkey species. Corcovado contains 2.5% of the world's biodiversity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition through the afternoon. Depending on your chosen route (San Pedrillo, La Leona, or Los Patos stations), wade through rivers, walk pristine deserted beaches, and explore diverse ecosystems from beach to dense jungle interior.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge exhausted but exhilarated. Enjoy a cold drink and a hearty dinner. Share wildlife stories with fellow travelers and review the incredible photos from the day. Early bedtime to recover.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast – a full meal to fuel the demanding jungle trek
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator or lodge – eaten in the jungle or on a beach within the park
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge dinner – fresh local fish, rice, beans, and tropical vegetables, $15–$20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires a licensed guide by law – book through your eco-lodge or a certified operator. Day treks cost ~$80–$120/person including guide and park fees. Wear long pants and long sleeves, waterproof boots, and heavy-duty insect repellent. Bring at least 3 liters of water. This is a strenuous full-day hike in intense heat and humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Osa Peninsula. Enjoy a slow, reflective breakfast at the eco-lodge. Take a short easy walk on the lodge's private trails for one last encounter with wildlife – scarlet macaws, toucans, and howler monkeys are commonly seen right on the property. Pack and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from the Osa Peninsula back toward San José via domestic flight from Puerto Jiménez airport (recommended, ~45 min with Sansa or Green Airways, ~$80–$120 one way) or by ground shuttle (5–6 hours). Arrive in San José with time to freshen up. Explore the Barrio Escalante neighborhood – San José's culinary and arts district – or visit the Jade Museum or the National Theatre.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner in San José to mark the end of an extraordinary 13-day Costa Rica adventure. Reflect on cloud forests, volcanoes, jungle canals, Pacific beaches, and the incredible biodiversity encountered throughout the trip. Head to the airport hotel or airport area accommodation for an early departure if needed.

meals.breakfast: Final eco-lodge breakfast – savor it slowly with jungle views
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Puerto Jiménez before the flight, or airport snack
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nuestra Tierra in San José – a beloved traditional Costa Rican restaurant with colorful décor and authentic cuisine, $15–$25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Domestic flights from Puerto Jiménez are strongly recommended over the long ground transfer – book weeks in advance as seats fill quickly. If departing Costa Rica on Day 14 or later, confirm your international flight and arrange airport transport. Allow extra time for San José traffic. Consider purchasing final souvenirs at the airport's duty-free or at the Mercado Central if time permits.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. With over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this adrenaline-packed experience offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including howler monkeys and toucans.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the lush rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of hanging bridges and trails. Walk at canopy level to observe exotic birds, howler monkeys, and tropical flora up close. The iconic cone of Arenal Volcano provides a dramatic backdrop throughout the hike.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and the rare squirrel monkey. The park also features stunning Pacific beaches where you can relax after the wildlife walk.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on a guided day trek through Corcovado National Park. Encounter tapirs, peccaries, giant anteaters, and all four of Costa Rica's monkey species in their pristine natural habitat. This remote and raw experience is the pinnacle of eco-adventure in Central America.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits at arrivals. Enjoy a chilled welcome drink and complimentary orchid lei in the vehicle. Check in to the Beachfront suite at Aegean Bliss Resort and unwind with a late-night turndown amenity.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort – curated welcome platter of Costa Rican cheeses, tropical fruits, ceviche, and a glass of premium Argentinian Malbec

day_by_day.notes: No activities scheduled before arrival. Confirm private transfer with resort concierge at least 48 hours prior. Keep Day 2 light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a private orientation tour of the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds with the head naturalist. Explore the resort's private beach, coastal gardens, and spot resident wildlife including howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, and white-faced capuchins in the surrounding trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling excursion along the resort's beachfront reef with a certified marine guide. Observe tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral formations. Return to the resort for a rejuvenating 90-minute couples' or solo rainforest-inspired spa treatment at the resort's luxury wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beachfront terrace. Private table dinner under the stars at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant – fresh tropical juices, gallo pinto, eggs benedict with plantain, and artisanal Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – ceviche de corvina, grilled fish tacos, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Signature oceanfront restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort – 4-course tasting menu featuring local lobster, heart of palm salad, slow-roasted pork tenderloin, and decadent tres leches cake

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally relaxed to allow recovery from international travel. Resort naturalist orientation is complimentary for premium guests – confirm with concierge upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Tour departing at 06:30 with a certified bilingual naturalist guide. Explore one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse national parks at dawn when wildlife activity peaks. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchins, squirrel monkeys, toucans, and nesting sea turtles along pristine white-sand beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided tour through the park's coastal trails, discovering poison dart frogs, Jesus Christ lizards, and magnificent frigatebirds. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by the resort on a secluded park beach. Return to the resort by 15:00 for free time and swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at the resort's jungle bar followed by dinner at a premium local restaurant in Manuel Antonio village.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-tour breakfast box prepared by resort – croissants, tropical fruit, hard-boiled eggs, and a thermos of Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic in Manuel Antonio National Park – charcuterie, artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: La Cantina Restaurant, Manuel Antonio – renowned for elevated Costa Rican cuisine; grilled mahi-mahi in mango-ginger sauce, hearts of palm ceviche, and local craft beer or premium wine

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap – book entry tickets well in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, insect repellent, and sturdy walking shoes. Binoculars provided by the naturalist guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs resort at 07:00 for Tortuguero National Park (approximately 4.5-hour scenic drive and boat transfer through jungle canals). Arrive and check in to a premium eco-lodge within the Tortuguero area for an overnight stay. Begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari in the afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – glide silently through the jungle canal network in a private electric boat with an expert naturalist guide. Spot caimans basking on riverbanks, river otters, green sea turtles, manatees, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including kingfishers, herons, and toucans.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a sunset cocktail on the riverside deck. Attend an optional guided night walk through the jungle to observe nocturnal wildlife including tree frogs, kinkajous, and bioluminescent insects.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure – fresh fruit bowl, eggs to order, and artisanal coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch at Tortuguero eco-lodge – Caribbean-style rice and beans, grilled snook, fried plantains, and fresh limeade
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the eco-lodge's restaurant – Caribbean lobster in coconut curry, cassava fritters, and passion fruit mousse

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small aircraft – the scenic canal journey is part of the experience. Pack a light rain jacket as the Caribbean coast receives frequent showers. February is nesting season for green sea turtles; a separate guided night turtle-watching tour can be arranged (subject to permit availability).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning second wildlife boat safari at dawn (06:00) when canal wildlife is most active – the misty morning light creates extraordinary photographic opportunities. Spot howler monkeys, sloths, and migratory bird species unique to the Caribbean coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat transfer back through the jungle canals to the mainland, followed by luxury vehicle transfer toward Arenal Volcano (approximately 3.5 hours). Check in to a premium eco-lodge with Arenal Volcano views. Enjoy the lodge's natural volcanic hot springs upon arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in private thermal hot spring pools with direct views of Arenal Volcano at dusk. Enjoy a premium dinner at the lodge's volcano-view restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the Tortuguero eco-lodge before departure – pastries, tropical fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch en route at a premium roadside restaurant in the Central Valley – casado with grilled chicken, black bean soup, and fresh fruit agua fresca
meals.dinner: Arenal eco-lodge signature restaurant – volcanic stone-grilled beef tenderloin, wild mushroom risotto, local cheese board, and a glass of premium Chilean Cabernet Sauvignon

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from Tortuguero to Arenal is long but scenic – request a comfort-class SUV with refreshments. Arenal Volcano is occasionally obscured by clouds; evening and early morning offer the best visibility. Bring a swimsuit for the hot springs.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Rainforest Hike – depart at 07:00 with a private certified naturalist guide. Trek through the lush primary rainforest surrounding Arenal Volcano on a network of suspension hanging bridges offering canopy-level views. Spot poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, coatis, and an abundance of orchids and bromeliads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hanging bridges circuit, crossing over dramatic ravines with views of the volcanic landscape and Lake Arenal. Return to the lodge by 13:30. Afternoon at leisure – optional kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal, or a private yoga session at the lodge's jungle platform.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat tour on Lake Arenal with champagne and canapés, watching the volcano's silhouette at golden hour. Return for a premium spa treatment followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Arenal lodge – açaí bowls, eggs benedict on plantain cakes, fresh Costa Rican coffee, and tropical juices
meals.lunch: Jungle picnic lunch during the hanging bridges hike – gourmet sandwiches, local cheese, tropical fruit, and sparkling water prepared by the lodge
meals.dinner: Restaurante Don Rufino, La Fortuna – one of Arenal's finest restaurants; grilled guapote fish, beef tenderloin in Salsa Criolla, and decadent chocolate volcano cake

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges hike involves moderate terrain – wear sturdy hiking shoes and long pants to protect against insects. The private guide will carry binoculars and a spotting scope for wildlife observation. Book the Lake Arenal sunset boat in advance through the lodge concierge.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on the Balsa River (Class II-III rapids) – a thrilling yet accessible adventure through lush jungle gorges near Arenal. Depart at 08:00 with a premium outfitter providing top-of-the-line safety equipment. Spot riverside wildlife including basilisk lizards, herons, and kingfishers between rapids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by 13:00. Afternoon visit to the Arenal Eco-Zoo for a private guided tour observing Costa Rica's most iconic reptiles and amphibians up close, including boa constrictors, caimans, and the famous red-eyed tree frog. Alternatively, enjoy a private canyoneering experience in the Arenal area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge's private thermal hot spring pools for a final volcanic soak. Premium dinner with volcano views.

meals.breakfast: Pre-activity breakfast at the lodge – energy-packed smoothie bowls, granola, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Post-rafting riverside BBQ lunch provided by the rafting outfitter – grilled meats, rice and beans, fresh fruit, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Private in-lodge dinner experience – chef's table for two with a 5-course tasting menu of Costa Rican fusion cuisine, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting on the Balsa River is suitable for most fitness levels. The chef's table experience must be booked at least 24 hours in advance through the lodge. This is the final night in the Arenal region – pack bags tonight for an early departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Early luxury transfer departs Arenal at 07:30 for Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3-hour scenic drive through mountain roads). Arrive at a premium cloud forest lodge and check in. Begin an afternoon of exploration in the misty cloud forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. Experience up to 13 cables, 3 suspension bridges, and a Tarzan swing with breathtaking views of the cloud forest and Pacific Ocean in the distance. The experienced bilingual guides ensure maximum safety and excitement.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory for a premium artisan cheese tasting paired with local wines and honey. Return to the lodge for a relaxing evening with cloud forest views.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure – full gourmet spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Santa Elena village – cloud forest mushroom soup, Monteverde cheese quesadillas, and fresh-brewed artisan coffee
meals.dinner: Celajes Restaurant at the cloud forest lodge – elevated Costa Rican cuisine with cloud forest views; cream of chayote soup, locally caught trout in herb butter, and guava cheesecake

day_by_day.notes: The mountain roads to Monteverde are winding and unpaved in sections – request a 4WD luxury vehicle. The zip-line tour requires closed-toe shoes and has weight restrictions (typically 100kg/220lbs maximum). Temperatures in Monteverde are cooler than the coast – pack a light fleece or jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided walking tour of the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve at 06:30 – the most biodiverse cloud forest in Central America. With a specialist ornithologist guide, search for the elusive resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and more than 400 other bird species amid ancient strangler figs and moss-draped trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Selvatura Adventure Park's butterfly garden, reptile exhibition, and hummingbird garden on a private guided tour. Observe more than 30 species of hummingbirds feeding at close range. Visit the cloud forest's famous orchid garden housing over 450 orchid species.
day_by_day.evening: Guided nocturnal cloud forest walk to observe night-active wildlife including kinkajous, tarantulas, sleeping birds, and tree frogs. Return to the lodge for a warming nightcap by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn continental breakfast at the lodge before the early bird walk – fresh fruit, pastries, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at Café Caburé, Monteverde – renowned for homemade chocolates and fusion cuisine; try the smoked chicken crepe and signature hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Tree House Restaurant, Santa Elena – dining inside a 100-year-old fig tree; grilled beef tenderloin, cloud forest mushroom pasta, and local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: The resplendent quetzal is most active during the February-April breeding season – this is an excellent time of year for sightings. Bring a telephoto camera lens for bird photography. The nocturnal walk requires a headlamp (provided by guides) and sturdy footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition – depart by private charter flight from Monteverde to Puerto Jiménez (approximately 1 hour) for a full-day expedition into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests. Arrive at Corcovado and begin the guided jungle trek with a specialized naturalist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado jungle expedition deep into primary rainforest. Encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, scarlet macaws, and if fortunate, a jaguar track or sighting. Explore pristine jungle rivers and dramatic coastal cliffs within the park. Return to Puerto Jiménez by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Private charter flight back to the Manuel Antonio/Quepos area (approximately 45 minutes) and luxury transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Welcome-back cocktail and dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure – packed for the flight
meals.lunch: Jungle picnic lunch during the Corcovado expedition – prepared by the expedition company; traditional Costa Rican rice and beans, grilled chicken, fresh fruit, and purified water
meals.dinner: Welcome-back dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant – fresh catch of the day, tropical salad, and a celebratory bottle of premium Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is a full-day commitment requiring an early start. The private charter flight eliminates the lengthy overland journey. Wear lightweight moisture-wicking clothing and waterproof boots. The Osa Peninsula has the highest biodiversity density on Earth – this is a once-in-a-lifetime wildlife experience. Permits must be arranged well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise catamaran sailing excursion departing from Quepos Marina at 06:30. Sail along the Pacific coastline with views of Manuel Antonio's jungle-clad hills. Spot spinner dolphins, humpback whales (February is peak season), and seabirds. Enjoy champagne and fresh fruit on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore by 11:00. Afternoon at leisure at Aegean Bliss Resort – private beach cabana with butler service, resort pool, or a premium spa treatment. Optional: private surf lesson on the resort's beach with a certified instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the resort's beach terrace. Premium farewell-to-the-Pacific dinner at the resort's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the catamaran – fresh tropical fruit, pastries, smoked salmon, and sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Gourmet beach club lunch at Aegean Bliss Resort – grilled shrimp skewers, ceviche trio, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Beachfront fine dining at Aegean Bliss Resort – 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing; highlights include yellowfin tuna tartare, grilled whole snapper, and a decadent dark chocolate fondant

day_by_day.notes: February is peak humpback whale migration season in Costa Rica's Pacific waters – the catamaran captain will know the best whale-watching zones. Book the spa treatment in advance as slots fill quickly. The private beach cabana with butler service should be reserved through the concierge the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Private horseback riding tour through the rainforest and coastal trails near Manuel Antonio, departing at 07:00. Ride through secondary forest, past waterfalls, and along clifftop trails with panoramic Pacific Ocean views. Experienced guides and well-trained horses ensure a safe and memorable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by 11:00. Farewell spa ritual – a 2-hour premium treatment package including a Costa Rican coffee body scrub, volcanic mud wrap, and relaxing full-body massage. Spend the remaining afternoon swimming, reading, or enjoying the resort's amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Private farewell dinner on the beach – the resort arranges a torch-lit table directly on the sand with a personal chef preparing a custom menu. Live acoustic guitar music accompanies the dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-ride breakfast at the resort – energizing smoothies, protein-rich eggs, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort – grilled fish bowl, tropical fruit sorbet, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private torch-lit beach dinner – custom 6-course menu by the resort's head chef; whole grilled lobster, beef tenderloin, local artisan cheeses, and a personalized dessert platter with 'Pura Vida' written in chocolate sauce

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner must be booked at least 72 hours in advance and is subject to weather conditions. If weather is unsuitable, the resort will arrange an equally intimate indoor alternative. Begin packing this evening as tomorrow is the final full day before departure preparation.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the resort's private beach to soak in the last moments of the Costa Rican Pacific coast. Optional early morning yoga session on the beach with the resort's wellness instructor. Leisurely final gourmet breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (late check-out arranged for 14:00 as a premium guest benefit). Luxury private transfer departs for Juan Santamaría International Airport (approximately 3-3.5 hours). Stop en route at a premium artisan market in San José's Escazú neighborhood to purchase high-quality Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the airport with ample time before departure. Access the premium lounge for refreshments and relaxation before the flight home. Carry memories of an extraordinary 13-day Costa Rican adventure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – the full gourmet spread; eggs any style, gallo pinto, tropical fruits, fresh pastries, and the finest Costa Rican single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at the resort or a quick gourmet stop en route to San José – fresh ceviche, plantain chips, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge dining or an early dinner at a top San José restaurant near the airport – Restaurante Grano de Oro, known for its elegant Costa Rican cuisine and legendary desserts

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late check-out with the resort concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3.5 hours for the drive to the airport to account for traffic. Purchase vacuum-sealed Costa Rican coffee and artisan chocolate at the airport duty-free as premium gifts. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations – do not purchase items made from protected species. Pura Vida!

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
